# onetsolutions_domain (Resource)

Registers a domain name for one year, a billed order that cannot be undone.

~> **Billing.** Creating this resource **places an order**: the domain is registered for one
year at the first-year price of its extension (see `onetsolutions_tlds`), paid from the account
balance. `terraform plan` checks that the name is available, refuses it otherwise with available
alternatives, and shows the price as a warning. Renewals are billed at `recurring_amount` while
automatic renewal is on.

!> **A registration cannot be undone.** A domain cannot be cancelled or refunded, so neither
`terraform destroy` nor a change of `name` deletes it: both **only remove it from the Terraform
state**, with a warning, and the domain stays registered, with its name servers and DNS zone,
until `expiration_date`. It renews, and is billed again, as long as automatic renewal is on: set
`auto_renew = false` in `onetsolutions_domain_settings` to let it expire. Protect the resource
with `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }`, or with `deletion_protection = true`, which refuses
the destroy and the replacement at apply time.

## What this resource manages

The order sets the name and the one-year registration, nothing else: it takes no contact
details, so the domain is registered with those of the organization's account, and its WHOIS
contacts are changed in the console. Everything that changes on a registered domain belongs to
`onetsolutions_domain_settings`: name servers, automatic renewal, registry lock and WHOIS privacy.
Point it at this resource's `id`, as in the example: Terraform then applies the settings after
the registration completes (for an order awaiting payment, apply again once the domain is
registered). This resource only reports `auto_renew`. The DNS zone of the domain is an
`onetsolutions_dns_zone`.

Only `deletion_protection` and `timeouts` change in place; a new `name` registers another domain.

## Registration and payment

The apply waits until the domain is registered (`status` becomes `active`), within the `create`
timeout. When the registration takes longer, the apply ends with a warning instead of an error:
the domain stays in the state, not tainted, and the next refresh reads its status. When the
registration fails, the apply fails and the resource is marked tainted, so the next apply orders
the name again; remove it from the configuration to stop.

When the account balance does not cover the order, the apply ends with a warning giving the amount
due and the payment link. The domain is in the state with status `pending` and is registered once
the invoice is paid in the console; the next refresh then reads it, and nothing is planned.

If the answer to an order is lost (timeout, server error), the apply stops without recording
anything in the state. The next plan finds the domain in the project if it was ordered, and asks
to import it rather than ordering it again.

A name already in the project is refused at plan time: import it instead (below).

## Deleted outside Terraform

When the domain is no longer in the project, the next refresh removes it from the state and the
next plan registers the name again, with the price warning.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Registers example.com for one year: a billed order that cannot be undone.
resource "onetsolutions_domain" "example" {
  name = "example.com"

  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}

resource "onetsolutions_dns_zone" "example" {
  zone_name = onetsolutions_domain.example.name
}

# The settings of the registered domain: delegation to the zone, renewal, lock and privacy.
resource "onetsolutions_domain_settings" "example" {
  domain_id     = onetsolutions_domain.example.id
  nameservers   = onetsolutions_dns_zone.example.nameservers
  auto_renew    = true
  locked        = true
  whois_privacy = true
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The domain name to register, lowercase without a trailing dot, such as `example.com`. Changing it registers the new name, and the previous domain stays registered.

### Optional

- `deletion_protection` (Boolean) Whether destroying (or replacing) the resource is refused. Defaults to `false`. Set it to `false` and apply before destroying a protected domain.
- `organization_id` (String) The organization the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `organization_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `project_id` (String) The project the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `auto_renew` (Boolean) Whether the domain renews automatically before it expires. Managed by `onetsolutions_domain_settings`.
- `dns_zone_id` (String) The UUID of the DNS zone attached to the domain, null when there is none.
- `expiration_date` (String) When the registration expires (YYYY-MM-DD), null until the domain is registered.
- `id` (String) The UUID of the domain.
- `next_billing_date` (String) The next renewal billing date (YYYY-MM-DD), null until the domain is registered.
- `recurring_amount` (String) The amount billed at each renewal, in EUR, as a decimal string.
- `registration_date` (String) When the domain was registered (YYYY-MM-DD), null until it is.
- `status` (String) The registration status: `pending` (ordered, not yet registered), `registering`, `active`, `expiring_soon`, `expired`, `suspended`, `transferring_out` or `failed`.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) How long to wait for the creation, as a duration such as "30s" or "2h45m". Defaults to `30m`.

## Import

A domain already registered in the project is imported by its UUID: the import orders nothing.
Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = onetsolutions_domain.example
  id = "3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/7d6c5b4a-3f2e-4d1c-9b8a-7f6e5d4c3b2a"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <organization_id>/<project_id>/<domain_id>, or <domain_id> when the provider sets organization_id and project_id.
terraform import onetsolutions_domain.example 3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/7d6c5b4a-3f2e-4d1c-9b8a-7f6e5d4c3b2a
```
